events.title: Drop client-side validation of tool results against the output schema
events.excerpt: `ClientSession.call_tool` checked every tool result's `structured_content` against the `outputSchema` from `tools/list`, using `jsonschema`. The server writes both the schema and the result, so the check could only tell you that a server disagrees with itself. It also cost a dependency tree (`jsonschema`, `jsonschema-specifications`, `referencing`, `rpds-py`) and an implicit `tools/list` the first time you called eac

events.title: fix: retry token refresh without RFC 8707 resource param when the AS rejects it
events.excerpt: ## Motivation and Context Fixes #2578. Microsoft Entra ID v2.0 rejects the RFC 8707 `resource` parameter on `refresh_token` grants (`AADSTS9010010`, strictly enforced since March 2026). Because the SDK sends it on every refresh, MCP clients using Entra OAuth lose authentication after ~1 hour: the silent refresh fails, tokens are cleared, and the user is forced through interactive re-auth every hour. events.excerpt: # fix(core-internal): classify an inbound JSON-RPC message by its envelope keys ## What `Protocol`'s `onmessage` now settles the message kind from its envelope keys before validating, so each inbound message runs one schema walk instead of three or four. - `result` or `error` → the result and error response schemas only. - `method` with `id` → the request schema only. - `method` without `id` → the notification schema

events.excerpt: The e2e `stdio` leg runs over `stdioClientOverPipes`, a test-only client on in-process pipes, instead of `StdioClientTransport`. Its `close()` only ended the server's stdin and never fired `onclose`, so `typescript:protocol:error:connection-closed` was listed as a known failure on stdio although the real transport passes it.
